3.text: His request, however, was not granted. After that, for three years Anadyr

4.text: again had no representative of the official authority. Only a few Cossacks,

5.text: from Petropavlovsk in Kamchatka, were sent to stay at Mariinsky Post. Life

6.text: there was quite wearisome. Thus one year no fuel was left for them by the

7.text: state steamer, and they were obliged to gather driftwood throughout the

8.text: winter from under the snow. They had no dogs, and had to drag their fuel

9.text: themselves on a sledge. They would go for fuel, and lose their way in a

10.text: snowstorm. Some of them told me, in speaking about this, “We knew nothing

11.text: about the country, and were sent against our will. We left our families in

12.text: Kamchatka. So, when we were in the greatest trouble, some one of us

13.text: would fling himself on the ground, and wail aloud (in old Russian fashion),

14.text: ‘Oh, my mother! why have you borne me for this trouble? O God! why

15.text: have you brought me to this country? Oh, we are wretched!’ etc.”

16.text: Then, in 1894, N. Gondatti — at present Governor of the Tobolsk

17.text: Province — was appointed chief officer of the Anadyr. He staid there three

18.text: years. Mr. Gondatti, who, like Maydell, was partly moved by scientific interests,

19.text: tried to imitate him also in his administrative activity. Thus he sent his
